subject: Procurement questionnaire — SLO measurement, alerting, and metrics access
messages:
From: Alicia Perez <alicia.perez@tesserahealth.com>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@tesserahealth.com>

Subject: Procurement questionnaire — SLO measurement, alerting, and metrics access

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked us to collect a short written response on how Redwood measures and exposes SLOs. Our security and SRE leads have three specific items: 

1) How does Redwood compute uptime and latency SLOs (windowing, rolling vs calendar, exclusion policy for planned maintenance)?
2) What monitoring/alerting thresholds do you recommend for customer-facing SLAs and can we see the alerts (or receive routed copies)?
3) Customer access to metrics: what dashboards, sampling windows, and retention will Tessera Health have access to? Are there roles (read-only / admin) and is there an audit trail?

We also need to understand the process for requesting a temporary sampling exception (we have a short reporting window that may need a relaxed sampling policy if we enable a large prefix-cache population). Can you return a concise packet by EOD Wednesday?

Appreciate it,
Alicia
Procurement Manager, Tessera Health

--
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Perez <alicia.perez@tesserahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire — SLO measurement, alerting, and metrics access

Hi Alicia — thanks for the note. Below is a short, direct response to each ask. I'm also attaching a one-page summary and a short README for inviting your dashboards. If you want a deeper technical packet we can schedule a quick call with our SREs.

1) How SLOs are computed- Uptime: calculated as the percent of API requests that complete (2xx/3xx) within the configured endpoint timeout over a rolling 30d window by default. We also publish a 7d rolling view for operational checks. We exclude scheduled maintenance if the customer is notified via the maintenance API and the window is recorded in the control plane.
- Latency: measured at the request level using p50/p90/p99 computed on server-side latency (time from request ingress to final token emitted). SLOs are normally expressed as p90 latency <= X ms over a rolling 30d window.
- Sampling & aggregation: we use full-sample telemetry for production shards by default; for ultra-high-volume customers we apply deterministic reservoir sampling that preserves tail metrics distribution for p90/p99 calculations.

2) Monitoring and alerting- We run multi-tier alerts: internal SRE alerts (paging) at breach of SLO-3m sustained (configurable) and customer-facing notifications for sustained degradations (>30m). Recommended thresholds are set per-route during procurement (we provide suggested p90/p99 targets based on model and profile). Alerts can be forwarded to a customer's PagerDuty and to a read-only incident feed in the customer dashboard.

3) Customer access to metrics- We provide a read-only dashboard with 7d/30d/90d windows, request-level sampling toggles for customers with reserved capacity, and export hooks (CSV/Grafana/Loki compatible). Role model: Org Admin (invite users, set routing), Viewer (metrics/read-only), Billing Admin (usage). All accesses are logged in the audit trail (retained 13 months by default).

Exception requests- For temporary sampling exceptions we require: stated time window, reason, expected traffic delta, and any compliance constraints. We can enable elevated sampling or relax prefix-caching exclusions for up to 72 hours with pre-approved ops mitigations. Longer exceptions require a short runbook and a CS/SRE sign-off.

Attachments: redwood-slo-measurement-summary.pdf (one-pager), dashboard-invite-instructions.txt

Let me know if that covers it or if you want more detail on sampling math or the reservoir parameters.

Best,
Rishi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Thanks Rishi — this is great and gets most of the way there. Two follow-ups from our SRE:

- Can you confirm the reservoir sampling method preserves unbiased p99 estimates (our concern is tail underestimation)?
- If we request a 72-hour sampling exception to capture a one-off migration spike, what controls will you put in place to guarantee no leakage of customer data into cached prefixes?

Also, please provide the dashboard invite for our monitoring team (viewer role) so they can poke around.

Alicia

Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire — SLO measurement, alerting, and metrics access

Looping in Jonas for SRE confirmation on sampling math and the data isolation control. Proposed internal note for procurement: we can state that our reservoir sampling is stratified by request class and deterministic per-customer session so p99 bias is constrained; we can include the formal proof excerpt if they want.

For the 72-hour exception, ops can enable a temporary prefix-cache blocklist (per-customer) plus a strict write-through policy for newly generated prefixes so nothing is eligible for cache-population during the exception window. This coupled with a short runbook (rollback steps + contact list) should satisfy compliance.

Jonas, can you confirm the above and add the standard wording for a 72-hour exception (what we need from the customer and what we commit to). Also Rishi, we should send the dashboard invite (viewer) now.

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. Product Manager, Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement questionnaire — SLO measurement, alerting, and metrics access

Hi Alicia — quick confirmations from SRE: 

- Sampling: our deterministic reservoir is keyed by customer-id and route; we maintain a bounded buffer that prioritizes tail latency events. In practice we run a simulated estimator during onboarding to validate p99 bias under representative load. We can share the simulator results under NDA or include a short technical appendix.
- Data isolation during exceptions: we will enable a per-customer cache exclusion rule and an immediate eviction protocol. During the 72-hour window we also turn on a strict audit mode (every cache write logged to the audit stream). Ops requires: request window, expected peak qps, and an emergency contact. We'll provide a template runbook and approve the request within 4 business hours of receiving it.

Dashboard invite: Alicia, I created a Viewer invite for your monitoring team and sent instructions to the email above. Invite link (expires in 7 days): https://app.redwood.ai/invite/eyJ0ZXN0Ijox.

If you want the short appendix on the sampling estimator, say the word and I'll attach it.

Regards,
Jonas
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
